value.assumption_check: THREE, named rather than resolved. (1) That an OpenAI-shaped client accepts a plain HTTP base_url with no TLS and no API key — MEASURED TRUE for hermes-agent 0.21.1 on 2026-09-11 and unmeasured for anything else; a client demanding TLS is the meeting shim's finding, not this machine's defect. (2) That non-streaming answers suffice — UNMEASURED, and paid for structurally: stream=true is refused BY NAME on the wire, so the assumption fails loudly the first time it is false instead of degrading into a hang. (3) That 'machine' is the right rung — a machine is tools plus glue and has no process of its own, which is exactly what this is: the process belongs to whichever shim includes it. Akien named the rung himself ('if you build it as it's own machine, then anybody can include it'), so this assumption has his word behind it, not mine.
value.builder_check: Wearing the cheapest-builder hat, FOUR questions the ticket must answer and now does. (1) 'What exactly is injected, and with what signature?' — resolve(request: dict) -> dict returning inference_domain's own resolve shape ({'answer': {...}, 'hit': bool, 'canonical': str}); models() -> iterable of model names. Both are constructor arguments, and the ticket spells the contract so the builder does not infer it from the spike's closure. (2) 'Where does the endpoint/model/temperature live?' — NOT HERE. The spike has module-level ENDPOINT/MODEL globals reading os.environ; those are the HOLDER'S, and their removal is named build work rather than left for the builder to notice. (3) 'How is a resolver failure answered?' — a named 5xx carrying the exception type, never a 200 with an empty choice; that is clause (c) and it has its own tooth. (4) 'Does serve.py bind a socket at import time?' — no; the handler class and a make_server(...) helper are separate, so the pure teeth can construct a handler with fakes and never open a port.
value.collision_check: TWO CHECKED, NEITHER TERMINAL. (1) The one-web-server rule — 'a device gets a declared PANE, never its own server'. Its WHY is that the UI must not fragment into per-device servers a human has to remember the ports of; this port serves a machine-to-machine wire format with no UI at all, and ruling 2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports settles it explicitly. A DISTINCTION TO RECORD, not a collision. (2) no-cross-device-imports (ruling 2026-08-31). Its WHY is that a device reaching into another device's internals bypasses the owner's gate; this machine imports NO device at all, which is strictly stronger. Also not a collision — and the check surfaced the missing_check finding above, because asking 'what enforces this?' is what revealed that nothing does.
value.falsifier_check: Stated in the ticket, five lettered clauses (a)-(e) so proof_coverage.clauses() demands a tooth per clause rather than falling back to [WHOLE] — a lesson taken from the sibling voyage 548dd13fb4db, where an unlettered five-clause falsifier would have been satisfied by one tooth. HORIZON: (a)-(d) are answerable the moment the machine exists and are the PROVEME bar; (e) — a real holder serving a real tool-using turn — is answered by cb97524c0e8e, which is why that ticket is this one's dependent rather than this one waiting on it. WRONG INTENT is the machine acquiring knowledge of inference_domain, the bus, or hermes.
value.missing_check: ONE POINT WAS NOT WRAPPED AND IS NOW. The falsifier's clause (a) — 'openai_wire imports no device' — had NO PHYSICS behind it. Measured during this cast: build_inspector's device_isolation_holds (inspector.py:3210) returns [] unless row['dir'] starts with 'devices/', so a file under cairn/machines/ importing cairn.devices.anything is caught by NOTHING today. That makes the machine's one load-bearing property a prose promise, which is the shape Law 4 calls an IOU. So the build carries a second piece: a machine_imports_no_device sieve beside its sibling, discovering machine dirs the way the existing one discovers device dirs. Without it this ticket ships a machine that is a device wearing a machine's name the first time somebody is in a hurry.

value.the_model_caveat_carried_forward: qwen3-coder:30b — the only model the shipped stack declares for chat — emits tool calls as TEXT on hex.local ollama 0.30.11, while qwen2.5:7b, llama3.2:3b and devstral-small-2:24b return them structured. That is a MODEL choice belonging to cb97524c0e8e, not a wire-format defect: this machine translates whatever the resolver returns.
value.the_physics_hole: build_inspector's device_isolation_holds (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py:3210) opens with `if not row['dir'].startswith('devices/'): return []`, so a file under cairn/machines/ importing cairn.devices.* is caught by nothing. Read directly from the source during the collision_check. The machine rung's meaning has been unenforced for as long as there have been machines; openai_wire is the first component whose value depends on it.
value.the_wire_shape: Taken off a real hermes-agent 0.21.1 on 2026-09-11, not from the schema in my head. The JSON-STRING arguments and the null content were both MEASURED refusals from ollama, and the evidence stays at CairnCommons/measurements/2026-09-11-hermes-openai-door-spike.py.

value.better_approach: Three looked at. (a) Put the port on inference_domain — SPECIFICALLY RULED OUT by Akien on 2026-09-11: 'not an openrouter port on the inference proxy. the shims handle all the interfacing with the outside world.' (b) Put the translation inside hermes_shim — simpler today and wrong tomorrow: the next OpenAI-shaped process (aider, any IDE assistant) would copy it, which is the stone-1 parallel-build failure. Akien closed this one himself: 'if you build it as it's own machine, then anybody can include it.' (c) Use an off-the-shelf proxy (litellm, openai-compatible shims) — it would dial the provider itself, which is the second door Law 6 exists to close, and it would not ride the bus.
value.hidden_assumption: That an OpenAI-shaped client will accept a base_url pointing at a plain HTTP port with no TLS and no key. MEASURED TRUE for hermes-agent 0.21.1 on 2026-09-11 (the spike served it), and NOT assumed for any other client — a client that demands TLS is a finding for the shim that meets it, not a defect here. A second assumption, stated because it is load-bearing and unmeasured: that a non-streaming answer is acceptable to the clients that will use this. stream=true is refused by name precisely so that assumption fails loudly instead of quietly.
value.prior_art: Consulted: the compiled intentions model (97 files, recompiled this act) has zero hits for openai, chat completion, or wire format; the ticket corpus has three hits and all three are this conversation's own siblings (548dd13fb4db, cb97524c0e8e, 328d61ee5101). In-house the nearest thing is cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py, which speaks ollama's /api/chat — the OTHER side of this translation, and the reason the machine is needed rather than a reason it is not. Outside: the OpenAI chat-completions schema is the prior art, and it is being IMPLEMENTED here, not reinvented — the shape came off the wire from a real hermes-agent 0.21.1, not from memory.
value.real_collision: Checked against the one-web-server rule (a device gets a declared PANE, never its own server) and it is NOT a collision — ruling 2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports settles that the rule governs the UI surface, not service ports, and this port serves a machine-to-machine wire format with no UI. Checked against 'no cross-device imports': this machine imports NO device at all, which is stronger than the rule requires and is clause (a) of its own falsifier.
